items.prompt:
Read the passage below.

Tomas walked the new student to every class on her first day so she would not get lost.

Claim A: Tomas helped the new student find her classes. Claim B: Tomas was the smartest boy in school. Which claim is supported by the text?
items.answer: Claim A is supported; the text shows Tomas walking her to every class. Claim B is an unsupported opinion the text never makes.

items.answer: Claim A is stated directly. Claim B is an assumption the text does not support.

items.prompt:

When the class pet died, Renata stayed after school to help bury it and made a small wooden marker, though she said little about it.

Claim A: Renata cared about the class pet. Claim B: Renata was the only student who was sad. Which claim is supported, and which goes beyond the evidence?
items.answer: Claim A is supported; Renata helped bury the pet and made a marker, showing care. Claim B goes beyond the evidence, since the text never compares her feelings to other students'.

items.prompt:
Read the passage below.

Hassan gave the last seat on the bus to an elderly passenger and stood for the long ride home.

Claim A: Hassan put the passenger's comfort first. Claim B: Hassan disliked sitting. Which claim is supported, and which is contradicted?
items.answer: Claim A is supported; he gave up the seat and stood. Claim B is contradicted by reason; he gave up the seat out of consideration, not dislike of sitting.

items.prompt:
Read the passage below.

After the team lost, the captain thanked every player by name before leaving the field, her voice steady.

Claim A: The captain wanted her teammates to feel valued. Claim B: The captain did not care about losing. Which claim does the evidence support?
items.answer: Claim A is supported; thanking each player by name shows she wanted them to feel valued. Claim B is not supported, since caring for teammates after a loss does not mean she did not care about losing.

items.prompt:
Read the passage below.

The clockmaker repaired the town clock for free his whole life. When the council finally offered to pay him, he refused, saying, 'I do not fix it for money. I fix it so no one is ever late to say goodbye.'

Claim A: The clockmaker saw his work as a service to the community. Claim B: The clockmaker needed the council's money. Which claim is supported, and why is the other contradicted?
items.answer: Claim A is supported; he fixed the clock for free and tied it to the community's needs ('so no one is ever late to say goodbye'). Claim B is contradicted, since he refused the payment.

Liora wrote the winning poem but signed it with her late grandmother's name, then slipped quietly out before the applause. She told no one why.

Claim A: The poem held a meaning tied to Liora's grandmother. Claim B: Liora did not write the poem herself. Which claim is better supported, and why is the other contradicted?
items.answer: Claim A is better supported; signing her grandmother's name and leaving quietly suggest the poem honored her grandmother. Claim B is contradicted, since the text states Liora 'wrote the winning poem.'
